One way to estimate the variance components
uses the mean squares from a one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) table
[@rocke2021epi204].
Write $\bar{Y}_{i\cdot} \eqdef \frac{1}{m}\sum_{j=1}^m Y_{ij}$ for the mean of group $i$
and $\bar{Y}_{\cdot\cdot} \eqdef \frac{1}{a}\sum_{i=1}^a \bar{Y}_{i\cdot}$ for the overall mean.
The **between-group mean square** and the **within-group mean square** are

$$
\ba
\text{MSA} &\eqdef \frac{m}{a-1}\sum_{i=1}^a \paren{\bar{Y}_{i\cdot} - \bar{Y}_{\cdot\cdot}}^2,
\\
\text{MSE} &\eqdef \frac{1}{a(m-1)}\sum_{i=1}^a\sum_{j=1}^m \paren{Y_{ij} - \bar{Y}_{i\cdot}}^2.
\ea
$$ {#eq-mean-squares}
